back: A productive suffix meaning 'can be'; examples include 'washable', 'disposable', and 'predictable'. [1]
Combines with nouns to describe people who consider one aspect of their lives especially important (e.g., 'health-conscious', 'class-conscious'). [1]
Used with names of famous people to form adjectives describing a similar style (e.g., 'Picassoesque'). [1]
Describes something without an undesirable aspect (e.g., 'stress-free', 'tax-free', 'additive-free'). [1]
Describes things with a lot of a particular substance (e.g., 'fibre-rich diet', 'calcium-rich foods'). [1]
Indicates something controlled or influenced by a specific group or person (e.g., 'community-led initiative', 'student-led protest'). [1]
Describes people with particular characters, opinions, or interests (e.g., 'like-minded', 'career-minded', 'money-minded'). [1]
Describes things that can resist damage or difficulty (e.g., 'waterproof jacket', 'soundproof room', 'idiot-proof'). [1]
Describes one thing as connected with another (e.g., 'stress-related absence', 'age-related earnings'). [1]
Describes people or things with a lot of something negative (e.g., 'guilt-ridden person', 'crime-ridden city'). [1]
Describes things that merit or deserve whatever the original noun refers to (e.g., 'newsworthy incident', 'praiseworthy action'). [1]
Can be used to describe a person who performs a specific action (e.g., 'applicant', 'informant', 'contestant'). [1]
Used to make adjectives from nouns (e.g., 'golden') or to make verbs from adjectives (e.g., 'moisten', 'sweeten', 'worsen'). [1]
While common for adverbs, it also forms adjectives like 'lively', 'costly', 'leisurely', and 'miserly'. [1]
A specific use of the '-ridden' suffix meaning a person has to stay in bed because they are ill. [1]
